text:
mira: quick idea: emit a tiny "client-accept" frame from edge -> client as soon as we accept the request payload (or persist it). purpose: surface a clear "accepted" UX state so clients avoid blind immediate retries and we can support a "suppress output" soft-shutdown to reduce duplicate work.

ben: is this a new wire-frame or are we reusing trailers / status frames?

mira: new small frame in our streaming protocol (single byte + optional metadata). semantics: accepted != completed. it only signals the request is routed/persisted.

alex: what exact UX/operational problems does this solve?

mira: three things: 1) UI can show "accepted" so users stop hitting retry, 2) on client cancel we can request upstream to keep computing but stop streaming tokens (suppress), 3) helps edge dedupe or cache quick retries.

sara: suppressing stream but letting computation continue sounds dangerous for side-effecting ops. we can't claim at-most-once.
mira: agreed. this is an optimization for stateless/generative calls. for side-effect endpoints we'd still require idempotency keys or forbid soft-suppress. route config can disable it.

jordan: billing question: do we bill on accept? or only when output tokens are produced?

alex: we should bill on output generation/completion. accept is just an event for UX/telemetry.

ben: failure cases: what if we ack to client then edge crashes before sending to backend? client believes accepted but request dropped.
mira: two choices: fast-accept (edge-local) or durable-accept (backend persistence). tradeoff latency vs correctness. recommend route-level opt-in: default to fast-accept for low-risk generation; durable-accept for critical routes.

sara: nice. can we make this explicit in SDK docs so integrators know not to retry immediately on accepted? maybe expose a `suggested_retry_ms` header in the accept frame.
mira: yes, SDK hint + header. default suggested_retry_ms = 1200ms (tunable). also add `accept_mode: fast|durable` in route config.

ben: implementation sketch for edge state machine?
mira: short pseudo: 
```
// states: RECEIVED -> ACCEPTED -> STREAMING -> SUPPRESSED -> COMPLETED
on receive: persist_or_claim(); send client_accept(); state=ACCEPTED
on upstream_start: state=STREAMING
on client_cancel:
  if state in {ACCEPTED, STREAMING}:
    send upstream {suppress_output:true}
    state=SUPPRESSED
    start timer T_suppress_ack
    if suppress_ack not received in T: escalate to hard-cancel
```

alex: need observability hooks: accept_sent, suppress_sent, suppress_ack, suppress_timeout, hard_cancel_escalation, duplicate_detected. make them sinkable to logs/metrics.

jordan: what about dedupe/cache? if accept + identical payload appears, edge could short-circuit if cached response available. TTL maybe short (seconds). keeper of cache keyed by body+params+route.

sara: also think about privacy: storing request body for durable-accept has retention implications. add config flag and KMS policy for durable-accept stores.

mira: good point. we'll add a retention policy and allow durable-accept only for routes explicitly allowed.

ben: operational rollout: feature flag + canary, need metrics: accept_rate, accept_latency, suppress_ack_latency, duplicate_retry_rate, escalation_rate.

ops-bot: deploy-plan: feature=client-accept, layer=edge, canary=5% -> 25% over 48h starting 1704300000. monitor: accept_latency_p50/p95, suppress_timeout_count, duplicate_event_rate.

jordan: i'll draft RFC w/ tradeoffs, security notes, and SDK changes (expose accepted flag + suggested_retry_ms). mira, you want to own the RFC?

mira: yep i'll take it and include sequence diagrams + state machine table. will post tomorrow. thanks for the quick feedback :thumbsup:
